_provenance: Captured live in DOSBox this session against PJOYG1.DAT (world 1, sublevel B).
Two disjoint tick ranges, gaps disclosed rather than filled. Segment A
correction below for why) was rebuilt in an earlier pass of this same
contiguous) was REBUILT FROM SCRATCH in a later pass -- see the correction
below. Every other tick in 0-404 was never captured live -- in particular
5-11, 18-21, 23-28 (segment A's own gaps) and the large stretch 31-157
(never captured at all, by either pass) are NOT filled in: several would
land in a proven-constant or linearly-bounded stretch and could be

independently read.
Each sample is {tick, heroX, heroY, state, camX, camY}.
Tick 0 (heroX=3424, heroY=608, camX=3296, camY=512) is independently
confirmed by full disassembly of FUN_1000_8c34 (CS:0x8FBE-0x8FC3): reached
from FUN_1000_006f's own init, gated by the one-shot DS:0x3e7 flag the joyg
cycler dispatch sets, it is what actually writes DS:0x3bd:=1 and
DS:0x282:=0 for joyg playback, hard-coding this exact hero/camera pair for
DS:0x3e6==2 (joyg1).
CORRECTION, earlier pass: the ORIGINAL segment A (ticks 0-18, contiguous)
sampled DS:0x282, DS:0x17a/0x17c, DS:0x377 and DS:0xa/0xc at an unpinned
point within each tick (a Lua wait_frames(1) poll, timed to whenever
DS:0x282 was observed to have changed -- see replay-diff.mjs's own header
for the full mechanism: a camera save/revert/restore dance at
CS:0x023C-CS:0x02E4, and a state-machine write at CS:0x0254 that simply
has not run yet if the poll lands early in the tick). Empirically this made
ticks 0-2 correct (the poll happened to land past both events) and ticks
3-18 each one recorded-input tick BEHIND where their own label claimed --
confirmed by direct comparison against a paired-read live rebuild, which
samples at CS:0x02F0 (after BOTH the camera final-restore and the
state-machine write, on every tick) and tags each reading by DS:0x282
itself rather than by poll timing. Because CS:0x02F0 supplies the LEAVING
value of the tick that just ran (hero/state) and the ENTERING value of the
NEXT tick (camera -- continuous, so leaving-T equals entering-T+1),
building one honest tick=T record pairs the camera field from the
cursor=T read with the hero/state fields from the cursor=T+1 read.
This correction is also what exposed and let that pass FIX two real port
bugs, both in gods-web/src/game/player.js's _ground(): (1) the original
enters the TURN_LR/TURN_RL pivot (CS:0x5DFE) on ANY first press from
ARRIVAL, not just a reversal -- ticks 14-15 (state 2 then 1, hero frozen)
were read by the OLD, wrongly-labelled capture as state 4 then 2, hiding
the pivot entirely; and (2) resuming a walk from a stopped pose also costs
one tick, via the same walk-state phase clamp (CS:0x5ACC-0x5AD3 /
CS:0x5D17-0x5D1E) undoing the resume tick's own step when phase holds the
stopped-pose sentinel (0x39/0x2d) -- ticks 29-30. See player.js's own
citations for the disassembly both rest on.
CORRECTION, later pass: segment B was REBUILT FROM SCRATCH via the SAME
CS:0x02F0/cursor-tagged/paired-read methodology segment A's own rebuild
used -- a single continuous, carefully-anchored live DOSBox session (two-
stage anchor to real tick 0 with no intermediate stop, then a conditional
execute breakpoint at CS:0x02F0 with DS:0x282==<target cursor> jumped
straight to each of 92 target cursor values in ascending order, zero
missed hits, zero cursor-tag mismatches across the whole run -- every
single read's own DS:0x282 matched the value its breakpoint's condition
asked for). DS:0x282 is a 16-bit WORD, not a byte -- segment A's own
cursor values never exceeded 30 so this never mattered before; segment B's
run up to 405 and MUST be read/compared as a word, not truncated to a
byte.
The going-in HYPOTHESIS for this rebuild was that segment B's OLD samples
carried the same unpinned-poll labelling bug segment A's did (both were
captured by the same discredited early-pass methodology). THAT HYPOTHESIS
IS REFUTED, not confirmed: the fresh, properly cursor-tagged live reads
reproduce the OLD file's own hero/state values almost exactly at every
sampled tick (e.g. old tick=166's {heroX:3764,state:1} matches this pass's
own cursor=167 read, {heroX:3764,state:1}, precisely the pairing this
convention predicts for an ACCURATE old reading, not a shifted one). The
OLD file's own camera field is the one place a small, consistent gap DOES
show up: old tick=166's camX=3556 versus this pass's freshly-paired
tick=166 camX=3560 -- exactly one camera-tick (4px) stale, the SAME
revert-window mechanism the tick-3 camera correction earlier in this file
documents, just recurring here rather than a new problem. Hero/state in
segment B was accurate all along; only its camera trailed by one tick.
What the rebuild found INSTEAD is a real, substantial divergence between
the port and the original across this whole range, present already at the
very first tick sampled (158: port heroX=3752, live=3736, a gap of 16px)
and growing to a gap of 148px by tick 403/404. Critically, the gap is NOT
a smooth accumulation -- it is a STAIRCASE: long stretches where the gap
is EXACTLY CONSTANT across many sampled ticks (16px flat across ticks
158-182 [24 ticks]; 68px flat across 200-286 [86 ticks]; 148px flat across
316-403 [87 ticks]). A flat plateau this long is strong, direct evidence
the port's OWN physics are correct for dozens of consecutive ticks at a
time -- this is not a pervasive per-tick bug.
Between the plateaus the gap grows in three places: +52px somewhere
within ticks 182-200, +28px within 286-300, and +40px within 300-311 --
all three of these growth windows were sampled only at their two
endpoints, so nothing beyond the TOTAL growth across each gap is known;
the exact tick(s) responsible, and whether each is one event or several,
is genuinely unresolved, not merely unstated. One piece of growth IS
pinned at single-tick resolution, because it happened to fall inside a
consecutively-sampled run rather than a gap: ticks 311->312 and 312->313
each show live heroX flat (3700, unchanged) while the port takes its own
ordinary +4px step (136->140->144 in the port-minus-live gap) -- two
individually-confirmed ticks where the port walks and the original does
not, not a sampling artifact. (Growth continues in some unresolved way
through 313-316 too -- tick 314 was not sampled -- but only that first
pair is pinned to single-tick resolution; treat 311-316 as ONE DENSELY-
SAMPLED WINDOW within the same class of unresolved growth as the other
three, not as a qualitatively different, more-exact finding.)
This shape -- long stretches of genuine lockstep, growth concentrated in
a handful of windows -- is most
consistent with something this replay harness (tools/replay-diff.mjs)
already discloses it does NOT model: objects/pickups/starburst/blocks/
debris are all null throughout, and trigger ACTION verbs never execute
(only selector 3's own condition evaluation runs). A pickup the recorded
path walks over, or a scripted trigger-driven pause/camera event, would
produce exactly this shape -- a real thing the harness can't see, not
necessarily a Player/Camera code bug. This is a LEAD, not a diagnosis:
nobody has yet live-investigated what specifically happens in the three
unsampled windows above (182-200, 286-300, 300-311), or the rest of the 311-316 growth beyond the two single-tick-pinned steps, to
identify the actual cause. Camera fields stay informational for this file
as a whole (see replay-diff.mjs's own header) -- not because of a
labelling risk (that hypothesis is now refuted for this file) but because
the SAME staircase pattern shows up in camX too, corroborating rather than
contradicting the hero-position finding.
